content.thinking:
I'm tracing the account page failures: shoppers hit errors from the start, with the logs showing ZeroDivisionError on those requests and warnings about the error rate. The cause is a divide-by-zero in spend_summary.py at line 47, and I still need to check what impact figures there are.

Now I'm checking the flag history: the monthly-spend feature began evaluating on for some requests around 02:55, yet the provider logged no flag change and no production changes in the hour before. So the trigger isn't in the change record, and I'm weighing whether a mixed-revision rollout could explain the split, since all three replicas ran one revision at that point.

I'm checking whether the flag provider's history explains the monthly-spend change, but it shows no flag changes by anyone except Argus in the hour before, even though the logs show the flag turning on around 02:55. I'm also noting that no deploy was recorded, though that absence alone doesn't rule one out.

I'm checking the flag history next: the monthly-spend flag's evaluations switched on around 02:55, but the provider's record shows no flag change by anyone except Argus in the hour before, so whatever switched it isn't in that record. I'm also noting that no earlier change is recorded, and that all replicas were running one revision, which makes a mixed-revision rollout unlikely as the split.

I'm reading the rest of the flag history now. The log rows show the monthly-spend flag turning on around 02:55, but the provider's record has no flag change by anyone except Argus in the hour before, so whatever switched it isn't in that record. I'm also checking the revision state: at the time of that read, all replicas were running a single revision, which argues against a partial rollout splitting traffic.

I'm working out why the flag flip doesn't appear in the provider's change history, and I'm noting that the logs put the monthly-spend flag at 26 on and 174 off at 02:55, with it fully on from 02:56. The roughly 30% error rate fits only idle shoppers failing, which I'll check against the code path next.

The divide-by-zero in spend_summary.py at line 47 is what's throwing, and it only triggers once the monthly-spend flag is on, since that path calls average_spend_per_item_this_month. That function divides the month's total by the count of this-month purchases with no zero check, so any shopper who has bought before but not this month hits it. The flag's switch-on isn't in the provider's change history, so what flipped it is still unrecorded.

I'm listing the contributing factors now: the flag switch never appeared in any change record Argus read, so Argus refused to act and it fell to a person. I'm also noting that nobody was paged, so no one could step in and turn the flag off.

I'm now weighing the fourth contributing factor: the flag jumped to full traffic quickly, with a small slice at 02:55 and everything on by 02:56, and no staged rollout stopped it on the error rate. Had it been held at the small slice, the failures would have stayed contained.

I'm weighing whether the rollout pattern should be a contributing factor too: the flag reached all traffic within a minute, and nothing paused it when the account page error rate climbed around 02:56. I'll record that as its own factor and propose tying flag rollouts to automatic reversion on error rate.

I'm weighing whether to recommend turning the monthly-spend flag off until the fix is merged, since that would stop the failures on the account page while the divide-by-zero remains in the code.

I'm turning to mitigation next: switching monthly-spend-feature off for io-shop until the fix is merged, since that would stop the failures while the divide-by-zero stays in the code. I'm also noting two process items: finding out how the flag got switched on without showing in the provider's history, and making every change to that flag go through the recorded history.

I'm listing the rest of the follow-up items: making every change to the monthly-spend flag go through the provider's recorded history so Argus can read and undo it, paging on-call when io-shop's error rate spikes, requiring flag-gated paths to be tested with the flag on, including shoppers with no purchases this month, and reverting the flag automatically when errors rise during a rollout. I'm also starting on the lessons, beginning with what went well: the investigator named the flag switch and the ZeroDivisionError as the top candidate and timed it, and Argus declined to act on a change missing from its record.

I'm weighing what went wrong in the investigation: the flag change never showed up in the change records I read, so the causes of the switch-on stayed unexplained, even though the logs show it happening at 02:55.

I'm weighing whether to note that nothing was done to stop the failures before Argus handed the incident to a person, so the flag stayed on while account pages kept failing. Argus stopping short was by design, but it's still a gap users felt.

I'm checking that the account page symptom is described plainly, with the cause stated as a likely failure in averaging for shoppers who have bought before but not this month. I'm also setting aside the ClientDisconnected errors, since they start before the flag change and look like unrelated background noise.

I'm working through the chain of events for the account page failures, starting from the failed shopper requests and the ZeroDivisionError they raised at spend_summary.py line 47. Next I'm laying out how the monthly-spend flag's evaluation changed around 02:55, which is the step I need to check against the record.

Now I'm going over the ruled-out causes, and I want to note that the record contains no earlier change I can dismiss, so I'll leave that line open.

I'm settling on the last step of the chain: turning the flag on sent account pages for shoppers with no purchases this month down a path that divides by their count of this-month purchases.

action_items.item: Turn monthly-spend-feature off for io-shop until the proposed fix is merged and deployed.
Find out how monthly-spend-feature was switched on without appearing in the flag provider's history or the production change events.
Make every flag change on io-shop go through the flag provider so it is recorded in the history Argus reads, and close any path that switches flags outside it.
Route the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to an on-call page.
Require tests that run each flag-gated code path with its flag on, including shoppers with past purchases but none this month, before the flag can be enabled in production.
Make flag rollouts on io-shop stage through traffic slices, and pause or revert automatically when the error rate rises.

causal_chain.step: The failing account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47. That error first appears in the logs at the onset and nowhere before it.

ruled_out.what: A revision rolled out to only some replicas, sending some requests down a different path: at {T10.1} all {T10.2} replicas ran one revision.

causal_chain.step: The monthly-spend-feature flag began evaluating on. Up to {G7e5d.4} every evaluation logged was off. At {G971b.6} some evaluations were on, and from {Gce95.4} the logs show it on. The switch appears in no change record Argus read: the production change events returned {T9.2} changes, and the flag provider's history showed {T15.2} flag changes by anyone but Argus. What switched the flag is not in the record. No deploy or other change was recorded, so none could be ruled out by the service being measured healthy with it in place.
Turning the flag on sent account pages for shoppers with no purchases this month down a code path that divides by their number of purchases this month.

input.cause_in_plain_words: A setting that adds a monthly spending summary to account pages came on, and nothing Argus read records who or what turned it on; the summary's code likely fails when it works out an average for shoppers who have bought before but bought nothing this month.

contributing_factors.factor: The switch of monthly-spend-feature to on was not recorded in the production change events or the flag provider's history, so Argus had no recorded change it could undo and refused to act on C1.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Had the switch been recorded, Argus could have turned the flag back off during the response. That would have stopped the failing account pages instead of leaving the flag on for a person to deal with.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: The alert paged nobody: no on-call incident was linked to it.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Once Argus left undoing the flag to a person, a paged on-call engineer could have turned the flag off and shortened the incident.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

contributing_factors.factor: No test was seen that exercised the flag-gated monthly summary for a shopper who has bought before but not this month before the flag was turned on. Code-Fix reports that the existing tests call this shopper the ordinary case and their own helper builds one.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A test like that would have raised ZeroDivisionError before the flag reached production, and the flag would not have been turned on with the fault in place.
contributing_factors.label: CF-3

contributing_factors.factor: The flag went from on for part of traffic to on for all of it, and no guard was seen that held or reverted it while the account page error rate rose.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A rollout held at the first slice, or reverted on the rising error rate, would have limited the failures to a small share of shoppers or ended them soon after they began.
contributing_factors.label: CF-4

went_well.item: The Investigator Agent placed the start of the incident at the minute the logs show the flag first evaluating on.
The Investigator Agent formed candidate C1, which named the monthly-spend-feature flag and the ZeroDivisionError the logs show.
Argus did not act on a change that was missing from the record of what changed, and left undoing it to a person.
The Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as draft pull request #540 for a person to review.

went_wrong: No mitigation was applied during the response: the flag was still on and account pages were still failing when the incident was escalated to a person.

input.root_cause: With monthly-spend-feature on, `render_spend_summary` calls `average_spend_per_item_this_month` (as long as `use_typical_spend` is false). That function divides the account's total for this month by the number of its purchases marked `in_current_month`, with no check for zero. A shopper who has bought before but not this month has no such purchases, so their account page request raises ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47.
input.still_at_risk: While monthly-spend-feature stayed on, account pages could keep failing for shoppers who had bought before but not this month, and the flag could be switched again without showing up in any change record Argus reads.
input.symptom: Account pages failed for some shoppers
